context: Reference coverage: a skill written from a one-round conversation about a Java lookup. A good answer writes a SKILL.md whose description names the task and the words a user would type, a hard stop that comes from the correction and nothing invented beyond it, a numbered workflow ending in a check, a references file with the not-like-this and like-this pair and the why, and one eval whose task is in another domain than the conversation, carries no hint of the answer, and weights the habit.

checklist.name: Writes the four files with valid front matter
checklist.description: Creates skills/<name>/SKILL.md with front matter holding a kebab-case name and a description, skills/<name>/references/examples.md, and one evals-reference/01-<slug>/ folder holding task.md and a criteria.json that parses as a weighted checklist.

checklist.name: Description names the task and the trigger words
checklist.description: The description says in the third person what the skill does (a lookup in a collection followed by an action on the found or missing element) and lists situations in the words a user would type, such as upsert, find-or-create, get-or-default, ending with a phrase like even if the user never says stream or Optional, and says what it is not for.

checklist.name: Hard stop traces to the correction
checklist.description: SKILL.md has one or two hard stops, and each is the correction the user made (no loop with an early return for a lookup; use a stream and the Optional API). No rule is added that the conversation does not support, such as rules about logging, naming, tests, or other Optional methods the user never mentioned.

checklist.name: Workflow ends in a check
checklist.description: SKILL.md has a numbered workflow whose last step is something the agent can tell is done, such as the method compiles and contains no loop and no early return.

checklist.name: References carry the pair and the why
checklist.description: references/examples.md shows the loop version under a not-like-this heading and the stream version under a like-this heading, in the conversation's own domain, with a one-sentence why taken from the correction.

checklist.name: Eval task is realistic, in another domain, and gives nothing away
checklist.description: The eval task.md is a prompt someone would type (a class with a collection and existing helpers, a method to add), uses a domain other than tickets and other than any example the written skill contains, and does not mention stream, Optional, findFirst, map, orElseGet, loops, or early returns.

checklist.name: Eval checklist weights the habit
checklist.description: criteria.json gives most of its points to the habit (stream lookup, Optional handling of both cases, no loop or early return) and a minority to compiling, preserved behavior and scope.

checklist.name: Nothing speculative or copied
checklist.description: The skill text does not quote the eval's class or method names, does not mention scores or scenarios, and does not promise behaviors the conversation never showed.
